sentences.zh: 【梁紀十三】　起旃蒙單閼，盡強圉大荒落，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 13] From Zhanmeng Danque through Qiangyu Dahuangluo; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 13] The span runs from Zhanmeng Danque through Qiangyu Dahuangluo—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十三大同元年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 13 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, thirteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元五三五年）

translations.literal: yimao, 535 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yimao, AD 535)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊申朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of wushen, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of wushen, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 是日，魏文帝即位於城西，大赦，改元大統，追尊父京兆王為文景皇帝，妣楊氏為皇后。

translations.literal: That same day, the Wei Emperor Wen took the throne west of the city, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Datong, and posthumously honored his father the Prince of Jingzhao as Emperor Wenjing and his mother Lady Yang as empress.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Emperor Wen of Western Wei was enthroned west of the city, proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Datong, and posthumously honored his father, the Prince of Jingzhao, as Emperor Wenjing and his mother Lady Yang as empress.

sentences.zh: 魏渭州刺史可朱渾道元先附侯莫陳悅，悅死，丞相泰攻之，不能克，與盟而罷。

translations.literal: Kezhunhun Daoyuan, governor of Weizhou in Wei, had earlier submitted to Houmochen Yue; when Yue died, Chancellor Tai attacked him but could not take him, made alliance with him, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhunhun Daoyuan, governor of Weizhou in Western Wei, had earlier sided with Houmochen Yue. After Yue died, Chancellor Yuwen Tai attacked him but could not overcome him; they made peace and Tai withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道元世居懷朔，與東魏丞相歡善。

translations.literal: Daoyuan's family had long lived at Huaishuo and he was on good terms with Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan's clan had long lived at Huaishuo, and he was on good terms with Gao Huan, chancellor of Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 又母兄皆在鄴，由是常與歡通。

translations.literal: Moreover his mother and elder brother were both in Ye, and for this reason he often communicated with Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother and elder brother were both in Ye, so he kept up regular contact with Huan.

sentences.zh: 泰欲擊之，道元帥所部三千戶西北度烏蘭津抵靈州，靈州刺史曹泥資送至雲州。

translations.literal: Tai wished to strike him; Daoyuan led his command of three thousand households northwest across the Wulan Ford to Lingzhou, and Inspector Cao Ni of Lingzhou supplied provisions and escorted him to Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai moved to attack him, Daoyuan led his three thousand households northwest across the Wulan Ford into Lingzhou; Inspector Cao Ni furnished supplies and saw him on to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 歡聞之，遣資糧迎候，拜車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Huan heard of it, he sent provisions to meet him on the road and appointed him Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Huan sent grain to welcome him on the road and appointed him Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 道元至晉陽，歡始聞孝武帝之喪，啟請舉哀制服。

translations.literal: When Daoyuan reached Jinyang, Huan had only just heard of Emperor Xiaowu's death and memorialized asking permission to observe mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang, Huan had only just learned of Emperor Xiaowu's death and memorialized asking leave to go into mourning.

sentences.zh: 東魏主使群臣議之，太學博士潘崇和以為：「君遇臣不以禮則無反服，是以湯之民不哭桀，周武之民不服紂。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei ruler had his ministers debate it. Erudite of the Imperial Academy Pan Chonghe held: "When a lord does not treat his ministers with ritual, the ministers owe no return-mourning—thus the people of Tang did not weep for Jie, and the people of King Wu of Zhou did not serve Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei court debated the question. Pan Chonghe of the Imperial Academy argued: "When a ruler fails his ministers in ritual, they owe him no mourning in return—just as Tang's people did not mourn Jie, and Zhou's people would not serve the tyrant Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」國子博士衛既隆、李同軌議以為：「高後於永熙離絕未彰，宜為之服。

translations.literal: Erudites of the National University Wei Jilong and Li Tonggui argued that "the late sovereign's break with Yongxi had not yet been made plain; mourning dress should be worn for him."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jilong and Li Tonggui of the National University held that, although the break at Yongxi was not yet public, the court should still go into mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 」東魏從之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei followed this view.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei followed their view.

sentences.zh: 魏驍騎大將軍、儀同三司李虎等招諭費也頭之眾，與之共攻靈州，凡四旬，曹泥請降。

translations.literal: Li Hu, Grand General of Valiant Cavalry in Wei, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes, and others rallied and instructed the Feiye Tou, and with them jointly attacked Lingzhou; after forty days in all, Cao Ni asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu, Western Wei's Grand General of Valiant Cavalry and Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, rallied the Feiye Tou and joined them in besieging Lingzhou. After forty days Cao Ni surrendered.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏進丞相略陽公泰為都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行台，封安定王；

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wei advanced Chancellor Duke of Lueyang Tai to Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Anding;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Western Wei promoted Chancellor Yuwen Tai, Duke of Lueyang, to Commander-in-Chief of All Armies, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner, and offered to enfeoff him as Prince of Anding;

sentences.zh: 泰固辭王爵及錄尚書，乃封安定公。

translations.literal: Tai firmly declined the princely title and the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and was therefore enfeoffed as Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Tai firmly declined both the princely rank and the recorder's post and was made Duke of Anding instead.

sentences.zh: 以尚書令斛斯椿為太保，廣平王贊為司徒。

translations.literal: He made Husu Chun, Chief of the Masters of Writing, Grand Guardian, and the Prince of Guangping, Zan, Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Husu Chun was made Grand Guardian, and the Prince of Guangping, Zan, Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏主立妃乙弗氏為皇后，子欽為皇太子。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Wei sovereign installed his consort Lady Yifu as empress and his son Qin as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Western Wei emperor installed Lady Yifu as empress and his son Qin as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後仁恕節儉，不妒忌，帝甚重之。

translations.literal: The empress was benevolent, forgiving, and frugal, free of jealousy; the emperor valued her greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was gentle, thrifty, and free of jealousy; the emperor held her in high regard.

sentences.zh: 稽胡劉蠡升，自孝昌以來，自稱天子，改元神嘉，居雲陽谷；

translations.literal: Liu Lisheng of the Jie Hu, since the Xiaochang era, had styled himself Son of Heaven, changed his era name to Shenjia, and dwelt in the Valley of Cloudyang;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lisheng of the Jie Hu, since the Xiaochang era, had called himself Son of Heaven, taken the era name Shenjia, and made his seat in the Valley of Cloudyang;

sentences.zh: 魏之邊境常被其患，謂之「胡荒」。

translations.literal: Wei's borderlands were constantly troubled by him; they called it "the Hu wasteland."
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei's frontier suffered constantly from his raids; people called the region "the Hu wasteland."

sentences.zh: 壬戌，東魏丞相歡襲擊，大破之。

translations.literal: On renxu, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan made a surprise attack and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Gao Huan struck by surprise and shattered his forces.

sentences.zh: 勃海世子澄通於歡妾鄭氏，歡歸，一婢告之，二婢為證。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng, heir of Bohai, had relations with Huan's concubine Lady Zheng; when Huan returned home, one maid reported it and two maids bore witness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng, heir of Bohai, had an affair with Huan's concubine Lady Zheng. When Huan came home, one maid denounced him and two others testified.

sentences.zh: 歡杖澄一百而幽之，婁妃亦隔絕不得見。

translations.literal: Huan beat Cheng a hundred strokes with the staff and confined him; Lady Lou was also cut off and could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had Cheng beaten a hundred times with the staff and imprisoned him; Lady Lou was barred from seeing him as well.

sentences.zh: 歡納魏敬宗之後爾朱氏，有寵，生子浟，歡欲立之。

translations.literal: Huan took in a descendant of Emperor Jingzong of Wei of the Erzhu clan, who won his favor and bore a son, You; Huan wished to install You as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Huan took a concubine from the Erzhu clan, a descendant of Emperor Jingzong; she bore favor and a son named You, and Huan meant to make You his heir.

sentences.zh: 澄求救於司馬子如。

translations.literal: Cheng sought rescue from Sima Ziru.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng turned to Sima Ziru for help.

sentences.zh: 子如入見歡，偽為不知者，請見婁妃；

translations.literal: Ziru entered to see Huan and pretended ignorance, asking to see Lady Lou;
translations.idiomatic: Ziru went in to see Huan and feigned ignorance, asking only to visit Lady Lou;

sentences.zh: 歡告其故。

translations.literal: Huan told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Huan told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 子如曰：「消難亦通子如妾，此事正可掩覆。

translations.literal: Ziru said, "Xiao Nan also had relations with Ziru's concubine—such a matter is exactly fit to be covered up.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru said, "Xiao Nan slept with one of my concubines too—affairs like this are meant to be hushed up.

sentences.zh: 妃是王結髮婦，常以父母家財奉王；

translations.literal: The consort is the king's wife of first marriage; she always used her parents' wealth to support the king;
translations.idiomatic: Your consort is the wife who bound up her hair with yours; she spent her family's fortune to keep you supplied;

sentences.zh: 王在懷朔被杖，背無完皮，妃晝夜供侍；

translations.literal: when the king was beaten at Huaishuo, his back had not a patch of whole skin, and the consort attended him day and night;
translations.idiomatic: when you were flogged at Huaishuo until your back was one raw wound, she nursed you day and night;

sentences.zh: 後避葛賊，同走并州，貧困，妃然馬矢自作靴；

translations.literal: later, fleeing the Ge bandits, you fled together to Bingzhou; in poverty the consort burned horse dung to make boots herself;
translations.idiomatic: later you fled the Ge bandits together to Bingzhou, and in poverty she burned horse dung to cobble boots for you.

sentences.zh: 恩義何可忘也！

translations.literal: How can such kindness be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: How can kindness like that be thrown away!

sentences.zh: 夫婦相宜，女配至尊，男承大業。

translations.literal: Husband and wife are paired: the woman is fit for the highest honor, the man to bear the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife belong together—the woman worthy of the highest place, the man to carry on the great house.

sentences.zh: 且婁領軍之勳，何宜搖動！

translations.literal: Moreover, what of the merit of the Lou clan's leadership of armies—how can it be shaken!
translations.idiomatic: And the Lou family's military merit—are you really going to unsettle that!

sentences.zh: 一女子如草芥，況婢言不必信邪！

translations.literal: A woman is like grass; besides, need the maids' words be believed!"
translations.idiomatic: One woman counts for nothing; and why believe servant-girls anyway!"

sentences.zh: 」歡因使子如更鞫之。

translations.literal: Huan therefore had Ziru investigate again.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had Ziru reinvestigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 子如見澄，尤之曰：「男兒何意畏威自誣！

translations.literal: Ziru saw Cheng and reproached him: "What sort of man cringes before authority and falsely accuses himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Ziru confronted Cheng: "What kind of man confesses under fear when he is innocent!"

sentences.zh: 」因教二婢反其辭，脅告者自縊，乃啟歡曰：「果虛言也。

translations.literal: He then taught the two maids to reverse their testimony, forced the accuser to hang herself, and reported to Huan: "It was indeed false."
translations.idiomatic: He coached the two maids to recant, drove the accuser to hang herself, and told Huan, "It was all lies."

sentences.zh: 」歡大悅，召婁妃及澄。

translations.literal: Huan was greatly pleased and summoned Lady Lou and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was overjoyed and summoned Lady Lou and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 妃遙見歡，一步一叩頭，澄且拜且進。

translations.literal: From afar the consort saw Huan and bowed her head at every step; Cheng bowed as he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lou saw him from afar and bowed with every step; Cheng advanced bowing as he went.

sentences.zh: 父子、夫婦相泣，復如初。

translations.literal: Father and son, husband and wife wept together and were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son, husband and wife wept and were reconciled as before.

sentences.zh: 歡置酒曰：「全我父子者，司馬子如也！

translations.literal: Huan set out wine and said, "He who preserved my father and son was Sima Ziru!"
translations.idiomatic: At a feast Huan declared, "Sima Ziru is the man who saved my house!"

sentences.zh: 」賜之黃金百三十斤。

translations.literal: He bestowed on him one hundred thirty catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him one hundred thirty catties of gold.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏以廣陵王欣為太傅，儀同三司-{万俟}-受洛干為司空。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Wei made the Prince of Guangling, Xin, Grand Tutor, and Moqi Shouluogan, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Western Wei made the Prince of Guangling, Xin, Grand Tutor, and Moqi Shouluogan, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 己巳，東魏以丞相歡為相國，假黃鉞，殊禮；

translations.literal: On jisi, Eastern Wei made Chancellor Huan Chancellor of State, with the yellow battle-axe and extraordinary honors;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Eastern Wei offered Gao Huan the post of Chancellor of State, the yellow battle-axe, and extraordinary honors;

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: he declined.

sentences.zh: 東魏大行台尚書司馬子如帥大都督竇泰、太州刺史韓軌等攻潼關，魏丞相泰軍於霸上。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru, Chief of the Masters of Writing of Eastern Wei's Grand Commissioner, led Grand Commander Dou Tai, Inspector Han Gui of Taizhou, and others to attack Tong Pass; Western Wei Chancellor Tai's army was at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru of Eastern Wei's Grand Commissioner led Grand Commander Dou Tai, Taizhou inspector Han Gui, and others against Tong Pass, while Yuwen Tai's Western Wei army held Bashang.

sentences.zh: 子如與軌回軍，從蒲津宵濟，攻華州。

translations.literal: Ziru and Gui turned their army, crossed the Pu Ford by night from the east, and attacked Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru and Gui swung back, crossed the Pu Ford by night from the east, and struck Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 時修城未畢，梯倚城外，比曉，東魏人乘梯而入。

translations.literal: At the time the wall repairs were not yet finished; ladders leaned outside the wall, and at dawn the Eastern Wei men climbed the ladders and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were still unfinished; scaling ladders stood against the outer face, and at first light Eastern Wei soldiers swarmed up them into the city.

sentences.zh: 刺史王羆臥未起，聞閣外匈匈有聲，袒身露髻徒跣，持白梃大呼而出，東魏人見之驚卻。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Pi had not yet risen; hearing a clamor outside the gate, he went out bare-bodied, hair loose, barefoot, wielding a white staff and shouting; the Eastern Wei men, seeing him, recoiled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Pi was still in bed when he heard uproar at the gate. He rushed out naked, hair loose, barefoot, swinging a white staff and roaring; the attackers fell back in shock.

sentences.zh: 羆逐至東門，左右稍集，合戰，破之，子如等遂引去。

translations.literal: Pi pursued them to the east gate; his attendants gradually gathered; they joined battle, defeated them, and Ziru and the rest withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pi chased them to the east gate until his men rallied; they fought, broke the enemy, and Ziru withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，上祀明堂。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinsi, the Liang emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 壬午，東魏以咸陽王坦為太傅，西河王悰為太尉。

translations.literal: On rewu, Eastern Wei made the Prince of Xianyang, Tan, Grand Tutor, and the Prince of Xihe, Cong, Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On rewu, Eastern Wei made the Prince of Xianyang, Tan, Grand Tutor, and the Prince of Xihe, Cong, Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 東魏使尚書右僕射高隆之發十萬夫撤洛陽宮殿，運其材入鄴。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent Chief of the Masters of Writing, Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi, to mobilize one hundred thousand laborers to dismantle the palaces of Luoyang and transport the timber into Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi to press one hundred thousand laborers into tearing down Luoyang's palaces and hauling the timber to Ye.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上耕籍田。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Liang emperor performed the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 東魏儀同三司婁昭等攻兗州，樊子鵠使前膠州刺史嚴思達守東平，昭攻拔之。

translations.literal: Lou Zhao and others, Bearers of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes of Eastern Wei, attacked Yanzhou; Fan Zihe sent Yan Sida, former inspector of Jiaozhou, to hold Dongping, and Zhao captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao and other Eastern Wei generals of equal rank to the Three Dukes attacked Yanzhou. Fan Zihe sent the former Jiaozhou inspector Yan Sida to hold Dongping; Zhao took the city.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵圍瑕丘，久不下，昭以水灌城；

translations.literal: He then led troops to besiege Xiaqiu; for long he could not take it, and Zhao flooded the city with water;
translations.idiomatic: He marched on to besiege Xiaqiu. The siege dragged on; Zhao diverted water to flood the town;

sentences.zh: 己丑，大野拔見子鵠計事，因斬其首以降。

translations.literal: on jichou, Daye Ba came to Fan Zihe to discuss affairs and thereupon cut off his head and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: on jichou, Daye Ba came to Fan Zihe on pretense of counsel, cut off his head, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 始，子鵠以眾少，悉驅老弱為兵，子鵠死，各散走。

translations.literal: At the outset, because his force was small, Zihe had driven out all the old and weak as soldiers; when Zihe died, each scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, short of men, Zihe had pressed every old person and child into service; when he died, they all fled.

sentences.zh: 諸將勸婁昭盡捕誅之，昭曰：「此州不幸，橫被殘賊，跂望官軍以救塗炭。

translations.literal: The generals urged Lou Zhao to seize and execute them all; Zhao said, "This province has been unfortunate, suddenly ravaged by brigands, and long looked to the official army to rescue them from fire and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged Lou Zhao to round them up and kill them. Zhao said, "This region has suffered enough—first bandits, now hoping for the government army to lift them out of misery.

sentences.zh: 今復誅之，民將誰訴！

translations.literal: If we kill them again, to whom will the people appeal!"
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter them now and whom can they turn to!"

sentences.zh: 」皆捨之。

translations.literal: He let them all go.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，司州刺史陳慶之伐東魏，與豫州刺史堯雄戰，不利而還。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Inspector Chen Qingzhi of Sizhou attacked Eastern Wei and fought Inspector Yao Xiong of Yuzhou; the outcome was unfavorable and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Sizhou inspector Chen Qingzhi invaded Eastern Wei and fought Yuzhou inspector Yao Xiong; beaten, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉，東魏以高盛為太尉，高敖曹為司徒，濟陰王暉業為司空。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinyou, Eastern Wei made Gao Sheng Grand Marshal, Gao Aocao Minister over the Masses, and the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinyou, Eastern Wei made Gao Sheng Grand Marshal, Gao Aocao Minister over the Masses, and the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡偽與劉蠡升約和，許以女妻其太子。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan feigned peace with Liu Lisheng and promised to give his daughter to Lisheng's crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan feigned peace with Liu Lisheng and promised his daughter to Lisheng's heir.

sentences.zh: 蠡升不設備，歡舉兵襲之。

translations.literal: Lisheng took no precautions; Huan raised troops and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: Lisheng let his guard down; Huan struck by surprise.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，蠡升北部王斬蠡升首以降。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Lisheng's northern king cut off Lisheng's head and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Lisheng's northern king beheaded him and submitted.

sentences.zh: 餘眾復立其子南海王，歡進擊，擒之，俘其皇后、諸王、公卿以下四百餘人，華、夷五萬餘戶。

translations.literal: The remnant host set up his son, the Prince of Nanhai, as ruler; Huan pressed the attack, captured him, and took prisoner the empress, the kings, the excellencies and ministers down to the fourth rank—more than four hundred persons—and fifty thousand households of Chinese and barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors enthroned his son, the Prince of Nanhai; Huan pressed on, seized him, and took the empress, princes, and more than four hundred officials, together with fifty thousand Chinese and non-Chinese households.

sentences.zh: 壬申，歡入朝於鄴，以孝武帝后妻彭城王韶。

translations.literal: On renshen, Huan entered court at Ye and gave Emperor Xiaowu's empress in marriage to the Prince of Pengcheng, Shao.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Huan came to court at Ye and gave Emperor Xiaowu's widow to the Prince of Pengcheng, Shao, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰以軍旅未息，吏民勞弊，命所司斟酌古今可以便時適治者，為二十四條新制，奏行之。

translations.literal: Western Wei Chancellor Tai, because the armies had not yet ceased and officials and people were worn with toil, ordered the relevant offices to weigh ancient and modern measures that could ease administration for the times, drew up twenty-four articles of new regulations, and memorialized them for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai, finding war unended and the people exhausted, ordered his offices to sift past and present for measures suited to the moment, framed twenty-four new regulations, and had them enacted.

sentences.zh: 泰用武功蘇綽為行台郎中，居歲餘，泰未之知也，而台中皆稱其能，有疑事皆就決之。

translations.literal: Tai employed Su Chuo of Wugong as Gentleman of the Mobile Headquarters; after more than a year Tai had not yet taken notice of him, yet everyone in the headquarters praised his ability, and doubtful matters were all brought to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Tai had appointed Su Chuo of Wugong as a clerk on the mobile headquarters staff. More than a year passed before Tai noticed him, yet the whole office praised his competence and brought him every hard case.

sentences.zh: 泰與僕射周惠達論事，惠達不能對，請出議之。

translations.literal: Tai was discussing affairs with Vice Director Zhou Huida; Huida could not answer and asked leave to go out and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was debating policy with Vice Director Zhou Huida; Huida could not reply and stepped out to think.

sentences.zh: 出，以告綽，綽為之區處，惠達入白之，泰稱善，曰：「誰與卿為此議者？

translations.literal: Going out, he told Chuo; Chuo worked out the disposition for him; Huida entered and reported it; Tai praised it and said, "Who debated this with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Outside he consulted Chuo, who laid out an answer; Huida went back in with it. Tai approved and asked, "Who worked this out with you?"

sentences.zh: 」惠達以綽對，且稱綽有王佐之才，泰乃擢綽為著作郎。

translations.literal: Huida named Chuo and also praised Chuo as having talent fit to assist a king; Tai thereupon promoted Chuo to Gentleman of the Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: Huida named Chuo and called him a man fit to aid a throne; Tai at once promoted him to the Writing Office.

sentences.zh: 泰與公卿如昆明池觀漁，行至漢故倉池，顧問左右，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Tai went with the excellencies to Kunming Pool to watch the fishing; passing the old Han storehouse pool, he looked back and questioned those at his side, but none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Tai took the high ministers to Kunming Pool to watch a fishing party. At the old Han storehouse pool he asked his attendants what it was; none knew.

sentences.zh: 泰召綽問之，具以狀對。

translations.literal: Tai summoned Chuo and questioned him; he answered in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Tai called Chuo, who gave a full account.

sentences.zh: 泰悅，因問天地造化之始，歷代興亡之跡，綽應對如流。

translations.literal: Tai was pleased and therefore asked about the beginning of heaven and earth's creation and the traces of successive rises and falls; Chuo answered like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Tai questioned him on cosmic origins and the rise and fall of dynasties; Chuo answered without pause.

sentences.zh: 泰與綽並馬徐行，至池，竟不設網罟而還。

translations.literal: Tai and Chuo rode side by side at an easy pace; when they reached the pool they did not set nets or traps and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They rode abreast at an easy pace; at the pool Tai never cast a net and turned back.

sentences.zh: 遂留綽至夜，問以政事，臥而聽之。

translations.literal: He kept Chuo until night and questioned him on government; he lay down to listen.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Chuo that night, questioning him on government while lying down to listen.

sentences.zh: 綽指陳為治之要，泰起，整衣危坐，不覺膝之前席，語遂達曙不厭。

translations.literal: Chuo pointed out the essentials of rule; Tai rose, straightened his robes, and sat upright; without noticing it his knees moved forward on the mat, and their talk lasted until dawn without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo laid out the essentials of rule. Tai sat up, straightened his robes, and listened formal and intent, knees edging forward on the mat, until dawn without tiring.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，謂周惠達曰：「蘇綽真奇士！

translations.literal: At the next court session he said to Zhou Huida, "Su Chuo is truly a rare man!
translations.idiomatic: Next day he told Zhou Huida, "Su Chuo is a remarkable man!

sentences.zh: 吾方任之以政。

translations.literal: I am about to entrust him with government."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to put the administration in his hands."

sentences.zh: 」即拜大行台左丞，參典機密，自是寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: He at once appointed him Left Director of the Grand Commissioner, participant in confidential matters; from this his favor grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately made him Left Director of the Grand Commissioner with access to state secrets, and favor only deepened.

sentences.zh: 綽始制文案程式朱出、墨入及計帳、戶籍之法，後人多遵用之。

translations.literal: Chuo first devised the documentary forms of red outgoing and black incoming, and the methods of ledgers and household registers; later men for the most part followed his usage.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo devised the red-out, black-in paperwork and the systems of accounts and household registers that later ages largely kept.

sentences.zh: 東魏以封延之為青州刺史，代侯淵。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei made Feng Yanzhi inspector of Qingzhou, replacing Hou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei appointed Feng Yanzhi inspector of Qingzhou in place of Hou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 淵既失州任而懼，行及廣川，遂反，夜，襲青州南郭，劫掠郡縣。

translations.literal: Yuan, having lost his provincial post and in fear, reached Guangchuan on the road and thereupon rebelled; by night he struck the southern suburb of Qingzhou and plundered the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed and afraid, Yuan rebelled on the road at Guangchuan, raiding by night the southern suburbs of Qingzhou and looting the surrounding districts.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丞相歡使濟州刺史蔡俊討之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Chancellor Huan sent Inspector Cai Jun of Jizhou to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Huan sent Jizhou inspector Cai Jun against him.

sentences.zh: 淵部下多叛，淵欲南奔，於道為賣漿者所斬，送首於鄴。

translations.literal: Many of Yuan's followers deserted; Yuan wished to flee south and on the road was beheaded by a man who sold gruel; his head was sent to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Much of Yuan's following deserted. He tried to flee south; a gruel-seller on the road cut off his head and sent it to Ye.

sentences.zh: 元慶和攻東魏城父，丞相歡遣高敖曹帥三萬人趣項，竇泰帥三萬人趣城父，侯景帥三萬人趣彭城，以任祥為東南道行台僕射，節度諸軍。

translations.literal: Yuan Qinghe attacked Chenfu in Eastern Wei; Chancellor Huan sent Gao Aocao with thirty thousand men toward Xiang, Dou Tai with thirty thousand toward Chenfu, and Hou Jing with thirty thousand toward Pengcheng, making Ren Xiang Vice Director of the Southeast Route Grand Commissioner to command all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qinghe attacked Eastern Wei's Chenfu. Huan sent Gao Aocao with thirty thousand toward Xiang, Dou Tai with thirty thousand toward Chenfu, and Hou Jing with thirty thousand toward Pengcheng, with Ren Xiang as southeast-route vice commissioner over all three columns.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏加丞相泰柱國。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wei added the post of Pillar of State to Chancellor Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Western Wei made Yuwen Tai Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 元慶和引兵逼東魏南兗州，東魏洛州刺史韓賢拒之。

translations.literal: Yuan Qinghe led troops to press Eastern Wei's southern Yanzhou; Han Xian, governor of Luo in Eastern Wei, resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qinghe advanced on Eastern Wei's southern Yanzhou; Luo governor Han Xian held him off.

sentences.zh: 六月，慶和攻南頓，豫州刺史堯雄破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Qinghe attacked Nandun; Yao Xiong, inspector of Yuzhou, defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he attacked Nandun; Yuzhou inspector Yao Xiong routed him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲戌，魏以開府儀同三司念賢為太尉，-{万俟}-受洛干為司徒，開府儀同三司越勒肱為司空。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiaxu, Wei made Kaifu Yitong Sanqi Nian Xian Grand Marshal, Moqi Shouluogan Minister over the Masses, and Kaifu Yitong Sanqi Yuelegei Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiaxu, Western Wei made Nian Xian Grand Marshal, Moqi Shouluogan Minister over the Masses, and Yuelegei Minister of Works—all with the rank of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史鄱陽王范、南梁州刺史樊文熾合兵圍晉壽，魏東益州刺史傅敬和來降。

translations.literal: Inspector Fan of Yizhou, the Prince of Poyang, and Inspector Fan Wenchi of southern Liangzhou combined forces to besiege Jinshou; Fu Jinghe, Eastern Inspector of Yizhou in Wei, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang prince Fan, inspector of Yizhou, and southern Liangzhou inspector Fan Wenchi jointly besieged Jinshou; Fu Jinghe, Eastern Wei's eastern Yizhou inspector, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 范，恢之子；

translations.literal: Fan was the son of Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Fan was the son of Hui;

sentences.zh: 敬和，豎眼之子也。

translations.literal: Jinghe was the son of Shuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe was the son of Shuyan.

sentences.zh: 魏下詔數高歡二十罪，且曰：「朕將親總六軍，與丞相掃除凶丑。

translations.literal: Wei issued an edict enumerating Gao Huan's twenty crimes, and also said, "We shall personally command the Six Armies, and with the Chancellor sweep away the vicious and vile."
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei published an edict listing twenty crimes of Gao Huan and declaring, "We shall take the field at the head of the Six Armies and, with our chancellor, wipe out this villain."

sentences.zh: 」歡亦移檄於魏，謂宇文黑獺、斛斯椿為逆徒，且言：「今分命諸將，領兵百萬，刻期西討。

translations.literal: " Huan also issued a proclamation to Wei, calling Yuwen Heitu and Husu Chun rebels, and saying: "Now I have assigned the generals to lead a million troops, with a fixed day to campaign west."
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan also sent a proclamation into Wei denouncing Yuwen Heitu and Husu Chun as traitors and declaring, "I have now assigned my generals to lead a million men west on a set day."

sentences.zh: 」東魏遣行台元晏擊元慶和。

translations.literal: " Eastern Wei sent Mobile Headquarters Yuan Yan to attack Yuan Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: " Eastern Wei sent Mobile Headquarters Yuan Yan against Yuan Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 或告東魏司空濟陰王暉業與七兵尚書薛琡貳於魏，八月，辛卯，執送晉陽，皆免官。

translations.literal: Some reported that Eastern Wei Minister of Works, the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, and Seven-Barracks Minister Xue Zan were double-dealing with Wei; in the eighth month, on xinmao, they were seized and sent to Jinyang, and both were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao, reports reached the court that Eastern Wei's Minister of Works, Prince Huiye of Jiyin, and Seven-Barracks Minister Xue Zan were dealing with Wei. Both were arrested and sent to Jinyang, then stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 甲午，東魏發民七萬六千人作新宮於鄴，使僕射高隆之與司空冑曹參軍辛術共營之，築鄴南城週二十五里。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Eastern Wei mobilized seventy-six thousand laborers to build a new palace at Ye, putting Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi and Registrar of the Ministry of Works Xin Shu jointly in charge; they built the southern wall of Ye, twenty-five li in circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Eastern Wei pressed seventy-six thousand laborers into building a new palace at Ye under Gao Longzhi and Xin Shu of the Ministry of Works. They raised the southern quarter of the city wall, twenty-five li around.

sentences.zh: 術，琛之子也。

translations.literal: Shu was Chen's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was the son of Chen.

sentences.zh: 趙剛自蠻中往見東魏東荊州刺史趙郡李愍，勸令附魏，愍從之，剛由是得至長安。

translations.literal: Zhao Gang came from the barbarian lands to see Li Min, Eastern Jingzhou inspector of Zhao commandery in Eastern Wei, and urged him to side with Wei; Min agreed, and Gang thereby reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gang came out of the barbarian country to Li Min, Eastern Wei's Eastern Jingzhou inspector in Zhao commandery, and persuaded him to join Western Wei. Min agreed, and Gang at last reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰以剛為左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai made Gang Left Household Gentleman with Grandee title.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuwen Tai made Gang Left Household Gentleman with Grandee rank.

sentences.zh: 剛說泰召賀拔勝、獨孤信等於梁，泰使剛來請之。

translations.literal: Gang urged Tai to summon Heba Sheng, Dugu Xin, and others from Liang; Tai sent Gang to request them.
translations.idiomatic: Gang urged Tai to call Heba Sheng, Dugu Xin, and the other exiles home from Liang; Tai sent him south to ask for them.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁巳，東魏以開府儀同三司襄城王旭為司空。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Eastern Wei made the Prince of Xiangcheng, Xu, Minister of Works with the rank of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Eastern Wei made Prince Xu of Xiangcheng Minister of Works with the rank of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏太師上黨文宣王長孫稚卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Grand Preceptor Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang, Changsun Zhi, died in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Western Wei's Grand Preceptor, Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang, Changsun Zhi, died.

sentences.zh: 魏秦州刺史王超世，丞相泰之內兄也，驕而黷貨，泰奏請加法，詔賜死。

translations.literal: Wang Chaoshi, governor of Qinzhou in Wei and Chancellor Tai's brother-in-law, was arrogant and greedy in office; Tai memorialized for the full penalty, and an edict ordered him to die.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chaoshi, Qinzhou governor in Western Wei and Yuwen Tai's brother-in-law, was arrogant and corrupt. Tai asked that the law be applied in full; an edict ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁未，侍中、中衛將軍徐勉卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingwei, Palace Attendant and Central Guard General Xu Mian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingwei, Palace Attendant and Central Guard General Xu Mian died.

sentences.zh: 勉雖骨鯁不及范雲，亦不阿意苟合，故梁世言賢相者稱范、徐雲。

translations.literal: Though Mian's backbone did not match Fan Yun's, he would not flatter and bend; therefore in the Liang age people who spoke of virtuous ministers named Fan and Xu together.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was not so unbending as Fan Yun, yet he never curried favor; Liang men who praised worthy ministers paired Fan with Xu.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，東魏主祀圜丘。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Eastern Wei ruler sacrificed at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the Eastern Wei emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 甲午，東魏閶闔門災。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Merchant's Gate of Eastern Wei caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Eastern Wei's Merchant's Gate burned.

sentences.zh: 門之初成也，高隆之乘馬遠望，謂其匠曰：「西南獨高一寸。

translations.literal: When the gate was first completed, Gao Longzhi on horseback looked from afar and told the craftsman, "The southwest corner alone stands an inch higher."
translations.idiomatic: When the gate was new, Gao Longzhi rode out to look and told the builder, "The southwest corner stands an inch too high."

sentences.zh: 」量之果然，太府卿任忻集自矜其巧，不肯改。

translations.literal: They measured it and it was indeed so; Minister of the Grand Commissariat Ren Xinji, gathering his pride in his skill, would not alter it.
translations.idiomatic: They measured and found it true. Ren Xinji of the Grand Commissariat, proud of his workmanship, refused to change it.

sentences.zh: 隆之恨之，至是譖於丞相歡曰：「忻集潛通西魏，令人故燒之。

translations.literal: Longzhi hated him; at this time he slandered him to Chancellor Huan, saying, "Xinji secretly communicates with Western Wei and had someone burn the gate on purpose."
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi bore a grudge and now told Gao Huan, "Xinji is in secret contact with Western Wei and had the gate set afire."

sentences.zh: 」歡斬之。

translations.literal: Huan executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had him executed.

sentences.zh: 北梁州刺史蘭欽引兵攻南鄭，魏梁州刺史元羅舉州降。

translations.literal: Lan Qin, governor of Northern Liangzhou, led troops to attack Nanzheng; Yuan Luo, Liangzhou inspector in Wei, surrendered the province.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Qin, governor of Northern Liangzhou, attacked Nanzheng; Yuan Luo, Western Wei's Liangzhou inspector, surrendered the whole province.

sentences.zh: 東魏以丞相歡之子洋為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封太原公。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei made Chancellor Huan's son Yang Cavalry General, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed him Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei made Huan's son Yang Cavalry General with the rank of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and enfeoffed him Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 洋內明決而外如不慧，兄弟及眾人皆嗤鄙之；

translations.literal: Yang was sharp and decisive within yet outwardly seemed dull; brothers and everyone else mocked and despised him;
translations.idiomatic: Yang was keen within yet seemed slow without; brothers and the rest sneered at him;

sentences.zh: 獨歡異之，謂長史薛琡曰：「此兒識慮過吾。

translations.literal: only Huan thought him extraordinary and told Chief Clerk Xue Zan, "This boy's insight surpasses mine."
translations.idiomatic: only Huan thought otherwise and told Chief Clerk Xue Zan, "This boy sees farther than I do."

sentences.zh: 」幼時，歡嘗欲觀諸子意識，使各治亂絲，洋獨抽刀斬之，曰：「亂者必斬！

translations.literal: When he was young, Huan once wished to test his sons' minds and had each untangle a mess of silk; Yang alone drew a sword and cut through it, saying, "What is tangled must be cut!"
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yang was tested with tangled silk like his brothers; he alone drew a sword and slashed it, saying, "Tangles are meant to be cut."

sentences.zh: 」又各配兵四出，使都督彭樂帥甲騎偽攻之，兄澄等皆怖撓，洋獨勒眾與樂相格，樂免冑言情，猶擒之以獻。

translations.literal: Again he assigned weapons to each to go out in four directions, and had Commander Peng Le lead armored horsemen in a feigned attack; the elder brother Cheng and the rest were terrified and broke, but Yang alone led his men to meet Le, who removed his helmet to speak his heart, and Yang still seized him and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan then gave each son troops and sent Peng Le to feign an attack. Cheng and the others panicked; Yang alone met Le in the field. Le doffed his helmet to plead, yet Yang took him prisoner and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 初，大行台右丞楊愔從兄岐州刺史幼卿，以直言為孝武帝所殺，愔同列郭秀害其能，恐之曰：「高王欲送卿於帝所。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mobile Headquarters Right Director Yang Yin's cousin, Inspector Yang Youqing of Qi province, had been killed by Emperor Xiaowu for blunt speech; Yin's colleague Guo Xiu, fearing his ability, frightened him, saying, "The Gao king means to send you to the emperor's court."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Yin of the mobile headquarters staff had seen his cousin Youqing, inspector of Qi, executed by Emperor Xiaowu for frank counsel. Guo Xiu, jealous of Yin's talent, warned him, "Prince Gao means to hand you over to the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」愔懼，變姓名逃於田橫島。

translations.literal: Yin was afraid, changed his name, and fled to Tianheng Island.
translations.idiomatic: Yin fled in terror, took a false name, and hid on Tianheng Island.

sentences.zh: 久之，歡聞其尚在，召為太原公開府司馬，頃之，復為大行台右丞。

translations.literal: After a long while Huan heard he was still alive, summoned him as staff officer to the Duke of Taiyuan's household, and soon restored him as Mobile Headquarters Right Director.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Huan learned he still lived, made him staff officer to the Duke of Taiyuan, and soon put him back in his old post.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，東魏文武官量事給祿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Eastern Wei civil officials received salaries according to the weight of their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Eastern Wei graded civil salaries by the burden of office.

sentences.zh: 魏以念賢為太傅，河州刺史梁景睿為太尉。

translations.literal: Wei made Nian Xian Grand Tutor and Liang Jingrui of Hezhou Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Nian Xian Grand Tutor and Liang Jingrui of Hezhou Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鄱陽妖賊鮮于琛改元上願，有眾萬餘人。

translations.literal: That year the bandit Xianyu Chen of Poyang changed his era to Shangyuan and had more than ten thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Poyang rebel Xianyu Chen took the era name Shangyuan and gathered more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽內史吳郡陸襄討擒之，案治黨與，無濫死者。

translations.literal: Lu Xiang, internal secretary of Poyang in Wu commandery, campaigned against him, captured him, and tried his party without a single wrongful execution.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiang of Wu, internal secretary of Poyang, defeated and captured him, then tried his followers without one unjust death.

sentences.zh: 民歌之曰：「鮮于平後善惡分，民無枉死賴陸君。

translations.literal: The people sang, "After Xianyu was pacified good and evil were sorted; the people owe no wrongful death to Lord Lu."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang, "When Xianyu fell, guilt was told from innocence; no man died wrongfully, thanks to Lord Lu."

sentences.zh: 柔然頭兵可汗求婚於東魏，丞相歡以常山王妹為蘭陵公主，妻之。

translations.literal: The Irkin of Rouran sought marriage with Eastern Wei; Chancellor Huan gave him the Princess of Lanling, sister of the Prince of Changshan, as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran's Irkin asked Eastern Wei for a bride; Gao Huan gave him the Princess of Lanling, sister of the Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 柔然數侵魏，魏使中書舍人庫狄峙奉使至柔然，與約和親，由是柔然不復為寇。

translations.literal: Rouran repeatedly raided Wei; Wei sent Palace Gentleman Kudizhi Shi as envoy to Rouran and arranged a marriage alliance, and thereafter Rouran no longer raided.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran had raided Western Wei repeatedly; the court sent Kudizhi Shi to treat for peace by marriage, and the raids ceased.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十三大同二年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 14 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fourteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元五三六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, 536 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, AD 536)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，魏祀南郊，改用神元皇帝配。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, Wei sacrificed at the southern suburb and changed the spirit tablet paired at the rite to the Divine Ancestor Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, Western Wei sacrificed at the southern suburb and paired the Divine Ancestor Emperor at the altar.

sentences.zh: 甲子，東魏丞相歡自將萬騎襲魏夏州，身不火食，四日而至，縛槊為梯，夜入其城，擒刺史斛拔俄彌突，因而用之，留都督張瓊將兵鎮守，遷其部落五千戶以歸。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan personally led ten thousand horsemen in a surprise attack on Xia province in Wei; he ate no cooked food for four days until he arrived, bound spears into ladders, entered the city by night, captured Governor Hubae Emi Tu, and employed him; he left Commander Zhang Qiong to garrison the city, moved five thousand households of the tribe away, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Gao Huan led ten thousand horsemen in a forced march against Western Wei's Xia province. Four days without cooked food brought him to the walls; spears lashed into ladders let his men in by night. He took Governor Hubae Emi Tu, kept him in service, left Zhang Qiong to hold the city, and resettled five thousand households before returning.

sentences.zh: 魏靈州刺史曹泥與其婿涼州刺史普樂劉豐，復叛降東魏，魏人圍之，水灌其城，不沒者四尺。

translations.literal: Cao Ni, governor of Lingzhou in Wei, and his son-in-law Liu Feng, governor of Liangzhou in Liang, rebelled again and surrendered to Eastern Wei; Wei forces besieged them and flooded the city, yet four chi of wall still stood above the water.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ni of Lingzhou and his son-in-law Liu Feng of Liangzhou rebelled again to Eastern Wei. Western Wei besieged them and drowned the town, yet four chi of wall still showed dry.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡發阿至羅三萬騎徑度靈州，繞出魏師之後，魏師退。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan sent thirty thousand horsemen of the Azhiluo to cross Lingzhou directly and circle behind the Wei army; the Wei army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent thirty thousand Azhiluo horsemen through Lingzhou to fall on the besiegers' rear; they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 歡帥騎迎泥及豐，拔其遺戶五千以歸，以豐為南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Huan led horsemen to welcome Ni and Feng, gathered five thousand remnant households, and returned; he made Feng governor of Southern Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan rode out to receive Ni and Feng, took five thousand surviving households, and made Feng governor of Southern Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 東魏加丞相歡九錫；

translations.literal: Eastern Wei offered Chancellor Huan the Nine Bestowals;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei offered Gao Huan the Nine Bestowals;

sentences.zh: 固讓而止。

translations.literal: he firmly declined and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: he refused firmly and the offer was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 上為文帝作皇基寺以追福，命有司求良材。

translations.literal: The emperor built Huangji Temple for Emperor Wen to gain merit and ordered the relevant offices to seek fine timber.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor built Huangji Temple for his father's soul and ordered officials to find noble timber.

sentences.zh: 曲阿弘氏自湘州買巨材東下，南津校尉孟少卿欲求媚於上，誣弘氏為劫而殺之，沒其材以為寺。

translations.literal: The Hong clan of Qu'e bought huge logs east from Xiangzhou; Commandant Meng Shaoqing of the Southern Ford, wishing to please the emperor, falsely accused the Hongs of banditry, killed them, and seized the timber for the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong family of Qu'e bought great timbers on the Xiang river route. Meng Shaoqing, commandant of the southern crossing, denounced them as bandits, had them killed, and took the wood for the temple.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai, the Liang emperor performed the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 東魏勃海世子澄，年十五，為大行台、并州刺史，求入鄴輔朝政，丞相歡不許。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng, heir of Bohai in Eastern Wei, aged fifteen, was Grand Mobile Headquarters and Bingzhou inspector; he asked to enter Ye to assist in government, and Chancellor Huan would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng of Bohai, fifteen years old, held Grand Mobile Headquarters and Bingzhou; he asked to enter Ye and help govern, and Huan refused.

sentences.zh: 丞相主簿樂安孫搴為之請，乃許之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Sun Cui of the chancellor's household pleaded for him, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cui, the chancellor's chief clerk, pleaded his case, and Huan yielded.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以澄為尚書令，加領軍、京畿大都督。

translations.literal: On dingyou he made Cheng Director of the Imperial Secretariat and added Colonel of the Garrison and Metropolitan Governor of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he made Cheng Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Colonel of the Garrison, and metropolitan governor of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 魏朝雖聞其器識，猶以年少期之。

translations.literal: Though the Wei court had heard of his talent, they still expected little because of his youth.
translations.idiomatic: The court had heard of his gifts but still thought him young.

sentences.zh: 既至，用法嚴峻，事無凝滯，中外震肅。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, his law was stern and nothing stalled; inside and outside were shaken into order.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, law was harsh and business never stuck; the whole administration snapped to attention.

sentences.zh: 引并州別駕崔暹為左丞、吏部郎，親任之。

translations.literal: He brought Cui Xian, assistant inspector of Bingzhou, in as Left Director and Director of Personnel and trusted him closely.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Cui Xian, Bingzhou's assistant inspector, as Left Director and Director of Personnel and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如、高季式召孫搴劇飲，醉甚而卒。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru and Gao Jishi summoned Sun Cui to drink heavily; Cui drank himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru and Gao Jishi drank with Sun Cui until he died of wine.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡親臨其喪。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan personally attended his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan came in person to his funeral.

sentences.zh: 子如叩頭請罪，歡曰：「卿折我右臂，為我求可代者！

translations.literal: Ziru kowtowed and asked forgiveness; Huan said, "You have broken my right arm—find me someone who can replace him!"
translations.idiomatic: Ziru kowtowed for pardon. Huan said, "You broke my right arm—find me another!"

sentences.zh: 」子如舉中書郎魏收，歡以收為主簿。

translations.literal: Ziru recommended Wei Shou, Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat; Huan made Shou chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru named Wei Shou of the Secretariat; Huan made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 收，子建之子也。

translations.literal: Shou was Zijian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was the son of Zijian.

sentences.zh: 它日，歡謂季式曰：「卿飲殺我孫主簿，魏收治文書不如我意；

translations.literal: Another day Huan told Jishi, "You drank my clerk Sun to death; Wei Shou does not handle documents as I wish;
translations.idiomatic: Another day Huan told Jishi, "You killed my clerk Sun with wine, and Wei Shou's papers still miss the mark.

sentences.zh: 司徒嘗稱一人謹密者為誰？

translations.literal: the chancellor once praised someone as careful and secret—who was it?"
translations.idiomatic: You once praised a man to the chancellor for care and discretion—who was he?"

sentences.zh: 」季式以司徒記室廣宗陳元康對，曰：「是能夜中闇書，快吏也。

translations.literal: Jishi answered with Chen Yuankang of Guangzong, registrar of the chancellor's household, saying, "He can write in the dark at night; he is a swift clerk."
translations.idiomatic: Jishi named Chen Yuankang of Guangzong, registrar on the chancellor's staff: "He can draft in the dark; a fast hand."

sentences.zh: 」召之，一見，即授大丞相功曹，掌機密，遷大行台都官郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned; at first sight he was made registrar of the Grand Chancellor in charge of secrets and soon promoted to Director of Capital Punishments on the Grand Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang was summoned, made the Grand Chancellor's registrar with secrets at once, and soon Director of Capital Punishments on the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多務，元康問無不知。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many; whatever Yuankang was asked, he knew.
translations.idiomatic: War and government pressed hard; Yuankang knew the answer to every question.

sentences.zh: 歡或出，臨行，留元康在後，馬上有所號令九十餘條，元康屈指數之，盡能記憶。

translations.literal: When Huan went out he left Yuankang behind; on horseback he gave more than ninety orders, and Yuankang counted them on his fingers and remembered them all.
translations.idiomatic: Huan would ride out leaving Yuankang behind and bark ninety orders from the saddle; Yuankang tallied them on his fingers and forgot none.

sentences.zh: 與功曹平原趙彥深同知機密，時人謂之陳、趙。

translations.literal: With Registrar Zhao Yanshen of Pingyuan he shared secrets; men called them Chen and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhao Yanshen of Pingyuan held the secrets together; people spoke of "Chen and Zhao."

sentences.zh: 而元康勢居趙前，性又柔謹，歡甚親之，曰：「如此人誠難得，天賜我也！

translations.literal: Yet Yuankang ranked above Zhao and was gentle and careful besides; Huan was very close to him and said, "A man like this is truly hard to get—Heaven's gift to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang outranked Zhao and was mild besides; Huan favored him and said, "Such a man is rare—a gift from Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」彥深名隱，以字行。

translations.literal: Yanshen's given name was Yin; he went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen's personal name was Yin; he used his style.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡令阿至羅逼魏秦州刺史-{万俟}-普，歡以眾應之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan ordered the Azhiluo to press Moqi Pu, governor of Qinzhou in Wei, and Huan himself brought an army in support.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent the Azhiluo against Moqi Pu, Western Wei's Qinzhou governor, and marched in support himself.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊申，丹楊陶弘景卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wushen, Tao Hongjing of Danyang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wushen, Tao Hongjing of Danyang died.

sentences.zh: 弘景博學多藝能，好養生之術。

translations.literal: Hongjing was erudite and skilled in many arts and fond of longevity techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing was learned, master of many arts, and devoted to longevity lore.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為奉朝請，棄官，隱居茅山。

translations.literal: He served Qi as a court gentleman, abandoned office, and lived in seclusion on Mount Mao.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Qi as court gentleman, then left office for Mount Mao.

sentences.zh: 上早與之遊，及即位，恩禮甚篤，每得其書，焚香虔受。

translations.literal: The emperor had long been his companion; when he took the throne his favor was thick, and whenever he received Hongjing's letters he burned incense and received them with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor had known him for years; on enthronement he honored him, and received each letter with incense and bowed head.

sentences.zh: 屢以手敕招之，弘景不出。

translations.literal: He repeatedly summoned him by personal edict, but Hongjing would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters called him again and again; Hongjing would not leave the mountain.

sentences.zh: 國家每有吉凶征討大事，無不先咨之，月中常有數信，時人謂之「山中宰相」。

translations.literal: Whenever the state faced omens or great campaigns, nothing was done without consulting him first; several letters a month passed between them, and men called him "the chancellor in the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: Omens and wars were never decided without his counsel; several letters a month passed, and men called him "the chancellor in the mountains."

sentences.zh: 將沒，為詩曰：「夷甫任散誕，平叔坐論空；

translations.literal: Before he died he composed a poem: "Yi Fu indulged in looseness, Ping Shu sat discussing emptiness;
translations.idiomatic: Near death he wrote: "Yi Fu wandered in license, Ping Shu sat debating emptiness;

sentences.zh: 豈悟昭陽殿，遂作單于宮！

translations.literal: who would have thought the Zhaoyang Palace would become the Xiongnu palace!"
translations.idiomatic: who dreamed the Zhaoyang halls would house the northern lords!"

sentences.zh: 」時士大夫競談玄理，不習武事，故弘景詩及之。

translations.literal: At the time gentlemen competed in discussing the abstruse and did not study martial affairs; therefore Hongjing's poem aimed at that.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen then traded in metaphysics and neglected arms; his poem struck at that fashion.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，東魏以華山王鷙為大司馬。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Eastern Wei made the Prince of Huashan, Zhi, Grand Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Eastern Wei made Prince Zhi of Huashan Grand Commander of the Army.

sentences.zh: 魏以涼州刺史李叔仁為司徒，-{万俟}-洛為太宰。

translations.literal: Wei made Li Shuren of Liangzhou Minister of Works and Moqi Luo Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Li Shuren of Liangzhou Minister of Works and Moqi Luo Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未，以驃騎大將軍、開府同三司之儀元法僧為太尉。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, Yuan Faseng was made Grand Commandant with the honor of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, Yuan Faseng was made Grand Commandant with the rank of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞考城江子四上封事，極言政治得失。

translations.literal: Jiang Zisi, Right Director of the Masters of Writing of Kaocheng, submitted a sealed memorial setting forth the gains and losses of government at length.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zisi of Kaocheng, Right Director of the Masters of Writing, sent a sealed memorial on the state of government.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸卯，詔曰：「古人有言，『屋漏在上，知之在下』。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guimao, an edict said, "The ancients had a saying, 'A leak in the roof above is known below.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guimao, an edict quoted the ancients: "What leaks in the roof, those below already know."

sentences.zh: 朕有過失，不能自覺，江子四等封事所言，尚書可時加檢括，於民有蠹患者，宜速詳啟！

translations.literal: "We have faults we cannot see for ourselves; what Zisi and the others wrote in their sealed memorials—the Masters of Writing should inspect them in good time and, where the people suffer harm, report swiftly!"
translations.idiomatic: "Where we err and do not see it, let the Masters of Writing weigh Zisi's words and report quickly every harm to the people!"

sentences.zh: 戊辰，東魏高盛卒。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Gao Sheng of Eastern Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Gao Sheng of Eastern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 魏越勒肱卒。

translations.literal: Yuelegei of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelegei of Western Wei died.

sentences.zh: 魏秦州刺史-{万俟}-普與其子太宰洛、豳州刺史叱干寶樂、右衛將軍破六韓常及督將三百人奔東魏，丞相泰輕騎追之，至河北千餘里，不及而還。

translations.literal: Moqi Pu of Qinzhou in Wei fled east with his son the Grand Mentor Luo, Binzhou Governor Chigan Baole, Right Guard General Poliuhan Chang, and more than three hundred commanders and generals; Chancellor Tai pursued with light horse more than a thousand li to the north of the river but could not overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Pu fled east with his son Luo, Chigan Baole of Binzhou, Poliuhan Chang of the Right Guard, and three hundred officers. Yuwen Tai chased a thousand li beyond the river and could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，東魏大赦。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, Eastern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, Eastern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上待魏降將賀拔勝等甚厚，勝請討高歡，上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor treated Heba Sheng and the other Wei defectors generously; Sheng asked to campaign against Gao Huan, and the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor treated Heba Sheng and the other Western Wei exiles well; Sheng begged to strike Gao Huan, and the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 勝等思歸，前荊州大都督撫寧史寧謂勝曰：「朱異言於梁主，無不從，請厚結之。

translations.literal: Sheng and the rest wished to return north; the former Grand Commander of Funing, Shi Ning, told Sheng, "Zhu Yi speaks to the Liang ruler and nothing is refused—cultivate him deeply."
translations.idiomatic: They longed for the north. Shi Ning, former grand commander of Funing, said, "Zhu Yi has the emperor's ear—win him first."

sentences.zh: 」勝從之。

translations.literal: Sheng followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng did so.

sentences.zh: 上許勝、寧及盧柔皆北還，親餞之於南苑。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted Sheng, Ning, and Lu Rou all to return north and personally saw them off with a feast at the Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let Sheng, Ning, and Lu Rou go north and feasted them farewell at the Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 勝懷上恩，自是見鳥獸南向者皆不射之。

translations.literal: Sheng cherished the emperor's kindness; from then on, whenever he saw birds or beasts heading south, he would not shoot them.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful thereafter, Sheng would not shoot any bird or beast flying south.

sentences.zh: 行至襄城，東魏丞相歡遣侯景以輕騎邀之，勝等棄舟自山路逃歸，從者凍餒，道死者太半。

translations.literal: When they reached Xiangcheng, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan sent Hou Jing with light horse to intercept them; Sheng and the rest abandoned their boats and fled by mountain paths; of their followers more than half died of cold and hunger on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng, Gao Huan sent Hou Jing with light horse to cut them off. They abandoned their boats and fled by mountain paths; more than half their party died of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 既至長安，詣闕謝罪。

translations.literal: When they reached Chang'an they appeared at court to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an they presented themselves to apologize.

sentences.zh: 魏主執勝手歔欷曰：「乘輿播越，天也，非卿之咎。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign grasped Sheng's hand, sighed and wept, and said, "The throne in exile is Heaven's doing—not your fault."
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei emperor took Sheng's hand, wept, and said, "Our exile is Heaven's will, not yours."

sentences.zh: 」丞相泰引盧柔為從事中郎，與蘇綽對掌機密。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai made Lu Rou attendant and participant in confidential matters, pairing him with Su Chuo to manage secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai made Lu Rou attendant with access to secrets, paired with Su Chuo.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬寅，東魏以定州刺史侯景兼尚書右僕射、南道行台，督諸將入寇。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renchen, Eastern Wei made Hou Jing also Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Southern Route Mobile Headquarters, supervising the generals in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renchen, Eastern Wei made Hou Jing Right Vice Director and southern-route mobile headquarters, commanding the invading columns.

sentences.zh: 魏以扶風王孚為司徒，斛斯椿為太傅。

translations.literal: Wei made the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, Minister of Works, and Husu Chun Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Prince Fu of Fufeng Minister of Works and Husu Chun Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙亥，詔大舉伐東魏。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, an edict ordered a great campaign against Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, Liang ordered a great campaign against Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 東魏侯景將兵七萬寇楚州，虜刺史桓和；

translations.literal: Hou Jing led seventy thousand men to raid Chuzhou and captured Governor Huan He;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing led seventy thousand men against Chuzhou, took Governor Huan He,

sentences.zh: 進軍淮上，南、北司二州刺史陳慶之擊破之，景棄輜重走。

translations.literal: advanced to the Huai, and Chen Qingzhi, inspector of the southern and northern Si provinces, defeated him; Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled.
translations.idiomatic: then pushed to the Huai. Chen Qingzhi, inspector of southern and northern Si, routed him and he fled without his train.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己亥，罷北伐之師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jihai, the northern expedition army was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jihai, the northern expedition was called off.

sentences.zh: 魏復改始祖神元皇帝為太祖，道武皇帝為烈祖。

translations.literal: Wei again changed the Divine Ancestor Emperor to Grand Ancestor and Emperor Daowu to Fierce Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei renamed the Divine Ancestor as Grand Ancestor and Emperor Daowu as Fierce Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，東魏以并州刺史尉景為太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Eastern Wei made Jing of Bingzhou Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Eastern Wei made Wei Jing of Bingzhou Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 壬申，東魏遣使請和，上許之。

translations.literal: On renshen, Eastern Wei sent envoys seeking peace, and the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Eastern Wei asked for peace, and the Liang emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 東魏清河文宣王但卒。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe in Eastern Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe died.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，東魏丞相歡督諸軍伐魏，遣司徒高敖曹趣上洛，大都督竇泰趣潼關。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan supervised the armies in campaigning against Wei, sending Minister over the Masses Gao Aocao toward Shangluo and Grand Commander Dou Tai toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Gao Huan took the field against Western Wei, sending Gao Aocao toward Shangluo and Dou Tai toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 癸未，東魏以咸陽王坦為太師。

translations.literal: On guimao, Eastern Wei made the Prince of Xianyang, Tan, Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Eastern Wei made Prince Tan of Xianyang Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏關中大饑，人相食，死者什七八。

translations.literal: That year Guanzhong in Wei suffered great famine; men ate one another, and seven or eight in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guanzhong in Western Wei starved until men ate men; seven or eight in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十三大同三年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 15 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fifteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 丁巳，公元五三七年）

translations.literal: dingsi, 537 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingsi, AD 537)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Liang emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡軍蒲板，造三浮橋，欲度河。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan's army was at Puban; he built three pontoon bridges, intending to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan camped at Puban and built three pontoon bridges to force a crossing.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰軍廣陽，謂諸將曰：「賊掎吾三面，作浮橋以示必度。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai's army was at Guangyang; he told the generals, "The enemy braces us on three sides and builds floating bridges to show he means to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai at Guangyang told his generals, "Huan pins us on three sides and floats bridges to say he will cross,

sentences.zh: 此欲綴吾軍，使竇泰得西入耳。

translations.literal: This is meant to tie up our army so Dou Tai can enter the pass to the west.
translations.idiomatic: but he means to hold us here while Dou Tai slips into the pass.

sentences.zh: 歡自起兵以來，竇泰常為前鋒，其下多銳卒，屢勝而驕，今襲之，必克。

translations.literal: Since Huan raised his army, Dou Tai has always been the vanguard; the troops under him are many sharp soldiers, and repeated victories have made them proud—strike now and you will surely take him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai has led every campaign; his men are the pick of the army and drunk on victory. Hit him now and you will have him.

sentences.zh: 克泰，則歡不戰自走矣。

translations.literal: Take Dou Tai and Huan will retreat without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Take Dou Tai and Huan will withdraw without a battle."

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「賊在近，捨而襲遠，脫有蹉跌，悔何及也！

translations.literal: The generals all said, "The enemy is near; to abandon him and strike far off—if we stumble, what regret will suffice!
translations.idiomatic: The generals objected: "The enemy is on our doorstep. Leave him for a distant foe and one misstep undoes us!

sentences.zh: 不如分兵御之。

translations.literal: Better to divide the army to defend."
translations.idiomatic: Split the army and defend each front."

sentences.zh: 」丞相泰曰：「歡再攻潼關，吾軍不出灞上，今大舉而來，謂吾亦當自守，有輕我之心。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai said, "Huan attacked Tong Pass twice and our army did not come out at Bashang; now he comes in force and thinks we too will only defend—he underestimates us.
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, "Twice Huan struck Tong Pass and we never left Bashang. He comes in strength expecting defense again—he underrates us.

sentences.zh: 乘此襲之，何患不克！

translations.literal: Seize this moment to strike—why fear we cannot win!
translations.idiomatic: Strike now—why should we fail!

sentences.zh: 賊雖作浮橋，未能徑度，不過五日，吾取竇泰必矣！

translations.literal: Though the enemy builds floating bridges, he cannot cross at once; within five days I shall surely take Dou Tai!"
translations.idiomatic: His bridges cannot cross in a day; within five days Dou Tai will be ours!"

sentences.zh: 」行台左丞蘇綽、中兵參軍代人達奚武亦以為然。

translations.literal: Mobile Headquarters Left Director Su Chuo and Staff Officer Daxi Wu of the Dai also held this view.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo on the mobile headquarters staff and Daxi Wu of the Dai agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，丞相泰還長安，諸將意猶異同。

translations.literal: On gengxu Chancellor Tai returned to Chang'an; the generals' minds were still divided.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Tai returned to Chang'an; the generals still wavered.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰隱其計，以問族子直事郎中深，深曰：「竇泰，歡之驍將，今大軍攻蒲板，則歡拒守而泰救之，吾表裡受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai concealed his plan and asked his cousin Shen, a gentleman on direct service; Shen said, "Dou Tai is Huan's fierce general; now the great force attacks Puban, so Huan holds fast and Dou Tai comes to rescue—we would be attacked front and rear; this is a perilous road.
translations.idiomatic: Tai hid his design and asked his cousin Shen. Shen said, "Dou Tai is Huan's hammer. While Huan holds Puban, Dou Tai will relieve him—we would be caught between two fires.

sentences.zh: 不如選輕銳潛出小關，竇泰躁急，必來決戰，歡持重未即救，我急擊泰，必可擒也。

translations.literal: Better to choose light, sharp troops to slip out by Xiaoguan; Dou Tai is rash and will surely come to a decisive battle; Huan is deliberate and will not rescue at once—we strike Dou Tai hard and can capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Send light, sharp men out by Xiaoguan. Dou Tai is hot-headed and will fight; Huan is slow and will not save him in time.

sentences.zh: 擒泰則歡勢自沮，回師擊之，可以決勝。

translations.literal: Capture Dou Tai and Huan's momentum will itself wilt; turn the army and strike him and the victory can be decided."
translations.idiomatic: Take Dou Tai and Huan's spirit breaks; wheel about and the day is won."

sentences.zh: 」丞相泰喜曰：「此吾心也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai was pleased and said, "This is my own heart."
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, "That is my own mind."

sentences.zh: 」乃聲言欲保隴右。

translations.literal: He then announced that he meant to secure Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: He announced he would secure Longyou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，謁魏主而潛軍東出，癸丑旦，至小關。

translations.literal: On xinhai he visited the Wei sovereign and then marched east in secret; on guichou at dawn he reached Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he took leave of the emperor and stole east; at dawn on guichou he was at Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 竇泰猝聞軍至，自風陵度，丞相泰出馬牧澤，擊竇泰，大破之，士眾皆盡，竇泰自殺，傳首長安。

translations.literal: Dou Tai suddenly heard the army had arrived and crossed from Fengling; Chancellor Tai came out at Horse-Pasture Marsh and struck Dou Tai, routing him utterly; soldiers and masses were all lost; Dou Tai killed himself, and his head was sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai heard too late and crossed from Fengling. Tai met him at Horse-Pasture Marsh, shattered his army, and Dou Tai killed himself. His head went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡以河冰薄，不得赴救，撤浮橋而退，儀同代人薛孤延為殿，一日之中斫十五刀折，乃得免。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan, because the river ice was thin, could not go to the rescue; he dismantled the floating bridges and withdrew; Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Xue Guyan of the Dai served as rear guard—in one day he broke fifteen swords and only then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Huan could not cross the thin ice to save him, broke up his bridges, and fled. Xue Guyan of the Dai covered the retreat and broke fifteen swords in a single day before he got clear.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰亦引軍還。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai also withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Tai withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 高敖曹自商山轉斗而進，所向無前，遂攻上洛。

translations.literal: Gao Aocao turned from Shangshan, fighting as he advanced; wherever he went none withstood him, and he thereupon attacked Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Aocao fought down from Shangshan without resistance and laid siege to Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 郡人泉岳及弟猛略與順陽人杜窋等謀翻城應之，洛州刺史泉企知之，殺岳及猛略。

translations.literal: Quan Yue of the district and his younger brother Menglue, with Du Yin of Shunyang, plotted to open the city in response; Governor Quan Qi knew of it and killed Yue and Menglue.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yue and his brother Menglue, with Du Yin of Shunyang, plotted to open the gates. Governor Quan Qi discovered it and killed the brothers.

sentences.zh: 杜窋走歸敖曹，敖曹以為鄉導而攻之。

translations.literal: Du Yin fled to join Aocao; Aocao made him local guide and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yin fled to Aocao, who used him as guide and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 敖曹被流矢，通中者三，殞絕良久，復上馬，免冑巡城。

translations.literal: Aocao was struck by stray arrows; three passed through his body and he lay unconscious a long while, then remounted, removed his helmet, and toured the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Stray arrows pierced him thrice; he lay senseless, then mounted again, bareheaded, and rode the circuit of the wall.

sentences.zh: 企固守旬餘，二子元禮、仲遵力戰拒之，仲遵傷目，不堪復戰，城遂降。

translations.literal: Qi held firm more than ten days; his sons Yuanli and Zhongzun fought hard to resist; Zhongzun was wounded in the eye and could fight no more, and the city thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held ten days. Sons Yuanli and Zhongzun fought hard until Zhongzun's eye was ruined; then the city fell.

sentences.zh: 企見敖曹曰：「吾力屈，非心服也。

translations.literal: Qi said to Aocao, "My strength is spent—not my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Qi told Aocao, "I yield from exhaustion, not from loyalty spent."

sentences.zh: 」敖曹以杜窋為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Aocao made Du Yin governor of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao made Du Yin governor of Luo.

sentences.zh: 敖曹創甚，曰：「恨不見季式作刺史。

translations.literal: Aocao was gravely wounded and said, "I regret not seeing Jishi made governor."
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, Aocao said, "Pity I never saw Jishi made governor here."

sentences.zh: 」丞相歡聞之，即以高季式為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan heard of it and at once made Gao Jishi governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Huan heard and at once made Gao Jishi governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 敖曹欲入藍田關，歡使人告曰：「竇泰軍沒，人心恐動，宜速還。

translations.literal: Aocao wished to enter Lantian Pass; Huan sent word, saying, "Dou Tai's army is destroyed and hearts are afraid; you should return quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao meant to enter Lantian Pass. Huan sent word: "Dou Tai is gone and the army shakes—come back at once.

sentences.zh: 路險賊盛，拔身可也。

translations.literal: The road is dangerous and bandits many—save yourself if you can."
translations.idiomatic: The road is bad and enemies thick—save yourself while you can."

sentences.zh: 」敖曹不忍棄眾，力戰，全軍而還，以泉企、泉元禮自隨，泉仲遵以傷重不行。

translations.literal: Aocao could not bear to abandon his troops; he fought hard and brought the whole army back, taking Quan Qi and Quan Yuanli with him; Quan Zhongzun, because his wounds were grave, did not travel.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao would not leave his men. He fought his way out with the whole column, taking Qi and Yuanli; Zhongzun, too hurt to ride, stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 企私戒二子曰：「吾餘生無幾，汝曹才器足以立功。

translations.literal: Qi secretly warned his two sons, "I have few years left; your talent and capacity are enough to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qi secretly told his sons, "I have little life left; your gifts are enough for great deeds.

sentences.zh: 勿以吾在東，遂虧臣節。

translations.literal: Do not, because I am in the east, then fail in a minister's constancy."
translations.idiomatic: Do not fail your duty because I am hostage in the east."

sentences.zh: 」元禮於路逃還。

translations.literal: Yuanli fled back on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli escaped on the road home.

sentences.zh: 泉、杜雖皆為土豪，鄉人輕杜而重泉。

translations.literal: Though Quan and Du were both local magnates, the villagers slighted Du and respected Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Du were both great houses, but the countryside honored the Quan and despised the Du.

sentences.zh: 元禮、仲遵陰結豪右，襲窋，殺之，魏以元禮世襲洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanli and Zhongzun secretly united with powerful men, raided Yin, and killed him; Wei made Yuanli hereditary governor of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli and Zhongzun rallied the gentry, ambushed Yin, and killed him; Western Wei let Yuanli inherit Luo.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dinghai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dinghai, the Liang emperor plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以尚書左僕射何敬容為中權將軍，護軍將軍蕭淵藻為左僕射，右僕射謝舉為右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On jichou, He Rongrong was made Central Guard General, Xiao Yuanzao Left Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xie Ju Right Household Gentleman with Grandee title.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, He Rongrong became Central Guard General, Xiao Yuanzao Left Director, and Xie Ju Right Household Gentleman with Grandee rank.

sentences.zh: 魏槐裡獲神璽，大赦。

translations.literal: In Wei a divine seal was obtained at Huaili, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei found a divine seal at Huaili and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛未，東魏遷七帝神主入新廟，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinwei, Eastern Wei moved the spirit tablets of seven emperors into the new temple and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinwei, Eastern Wei installed seven imperial tablets in the new temple and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏斛斯椿卒。

translations.literal: Husu Chun of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Husu Chun of Western Wei died.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，魏以廣陵王欣為太宰，賀拔勝為太師。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Wei made the Prince of Guangling, Xin, Grand Mentor, and Heba Sheng Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Western Wei made Prince Xin of Guangling Grand Mentor and Heba Sheng Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏以扶風王孚為太保，梁景睿為太傅，廣平王贊為太尉，開府儀同三司武川王盟為司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wei made the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, Grand Protector, Liang Jingrui Grand Tutor, the Prince of Guangping, Zan, Grand Commandant, and Wang Meng of Wuchuan Minister of Works with the rank of Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
